name: Synthesis Tutor
line: Synthesis Tutor teaches in short lessons on one idea. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review happen at every problem.
description: AMP vs Synthesis Tutor: Synthesis teaches in short voiced lessons, one idea each. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous, at every problem.
verdict: Synthesis Tutor teaches in short lessons on one idea each, guided by a tutor's voice, and checks inside each lesson decide when a child moves on [1][5]. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous. Every answer updates the learner's level and sets the next problem, and each problem carries its own hint, lesson and worked answer.

reasons.title: The problem is the unit
reasons.body: In AMP, everything hangs off the problem in front of the learner: a hint that gives the first step, a lesson with a worked example, a video lesson, the worked answer afterward, and links to the skills it builds on and leads to. In Synthesis Tutor the unit is the lesson: a few minutes on one idea, guided by a tutor's voice, that starts with action on screen and moves to symbols after [1][4][5]. Across 55 studies, worked examples improve performance in math [11].

reasons.title: Continuous assessment
reasons.body: AMP has no separate test. It places a learner from their first answers, and every answer after updates the learner's level and sets the next problem: new work within reach, a gap to close, or an old skill due back. In Synthesis Tutor, short checks inside each lesson decide when the child moves on. The next lesson is chosen by the child from a map, or by a lesson planner [1].

reasons.title: Moving on, and going back
reasons.body: In AMP a skill counts when the learner gets it right without help, more than once. An answer given after a hint or a lesson is marked as helped and does not count as learned. Repeated misses send practice back to what the skill builds on. Synthesis says a child moves on in a lesson or unit once they show they have understood and mastered the material, and that its instruction targets gaps in knowledge [1].

reasons.title: Continuous review
reasons.body: In AMP, learned skills come back in ordinary practice, at growing intervals, mixed with other math. Synthesis Tutor teaches one idea in each lesson, and short checks inside the lesson decide when the child moves on to new material [1][5]. We found no scheduled return to earlier lessons in the Synthesis pages we read [1][2][3]. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% on the researchers' test a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [10].

reasons.title: One map from counting through precalculus
reasons.body: AMP is one program from counting through precalculus, on one map of skills. It keeps a separate level for each part of math, so a learner further along in one part than another gets work at both levels. Synthesis Tutor is designed for ages 5 to 11 and covers the standard kindergarten through grade 5 curriculum [1].

rows.range: Ages 5 to 11: the standard kindergarten through grade 5 curriculum, from counting to fractions and algebraic thinking [1].
rows.start: Placement checks, or the child picks a lesson from a map [1].
rows.teaching: Short lessons on one idea, guided by a tutor's voice, starting with action on screen before symbols [1][4][5].
rows.next: A lesson planner, or the child's own choice from a map. Inside a lesson, checks decide when the child moves on [1].
rows.mastery: The child moves on once they show they have understood and mastered the material [1].
rows.review: No scheduled review of earlier lessons found in the pages we read [1][2][3].
rows.print: No workbooks or printables found in the pages we read [1][2][3].
rows.adult: Little. The maker calls it hands-off for parents and teachers. Adults set up accounts and read reports [1].
rows.reports: Progress reports, session summaries and weekly progress emails [1].
rows.evidence: No outcome study found on its site, in Evidence for ESSA or in the What Works Clearinghouse [6][8][9].

theirs: Synthesis Tutor is made by Synthesis, a California company founded in 2020. It grew out of a class at an experimental school started on the SpaceX campus [2]. The tutor is designed for ages 5 to 11 and covers the standard kindergarten through grade 5 curriculum [1]. Its maker says it is not ChatGPT [1].

A lesson runs a few minutes and teaches one idea [5]. A tutor's voice guides every problem while the child acts on the screen, and each topic starts with hands-on action before symbols [1][4]. Short checks inside the lesson decide when the child moves on [1]. The child picks the next lesson from a map, or a lesson planner picks it [1]. For children under 7, every word and answer choice is read aloud [1].
credit: Each topic starts with hands-on action on screen before symbols [4].
Made for young children. Everything is read aloud for children under 7 [1].

theirs: We found no outcome study of Synthesis Tutor on its site. It has no entry in Evidence for ESSA or the What Works Clearinghouse [8][9].

Synthesis's blog post on whether Synthesis Tutor gets results reports no data from Synthesis Tutor. It describes the DARPA Digital Tutor and says Synthesis partnered with the team that built it [6]. A 2020 summary that Synthesis links describes that program as a tutor built around 2009 to train new Navy recruits as IT workers. The summary gives no number of students in each group and does not say how they were assigned [7].
Its page for schools states that 98% of teachers reported improved math skills, with no source, sample or date given [3].
ours: Two findings bear most on this comparison. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders that meets What Works Clearinghouse standards without reservations, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% on the researchers' test a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [10]. Across 55 studies, worked examples improve performance in math [11]. AMP applies both at every problem.

AMP's own outcome studies are planned: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. The research behind each part of AMP is in our report, and AMP is open source.

them: You want a young child to learn in short lessons, guided by a tutor's voice, that start with action on screen.
amp: You want assessment, teaching and review in the same practice, with no separate tests.
You want a hint, a lesson and the worked answer at every problem.
You want learned skills to keep coming back in practice.
Your child is at different levels in different parts of math, or will need math past grade 5.

questions.question: How is AMP different from Synthesis Tutor?
questions.answer: Synthesis Tutor teaches in short lessons on one idea each, and moves a child on once they show understanding [1][5]. In AMP the problem is the unit: every answer sets the next problem, each problem carries its own teaching, and learned skills return in ordinary practice.

questions.question: Does Synthesis Tutor work?
questions.answer: We found no outcome study of Synthesis Tutor on its site, in Evidence for ESSA or in the What Works Clearinghouse [8][9]. Its post on results describes a different program, the DARPA Digital Tutor, built to train Navy recruits as IT workers [6][7].

questions.question: Can a learner use both?
questions.answer: Yes. They are separate programs. AMP places a learner from their first answers, whatever else they use.
